home-remodeling.local_heading: A city that finished, then started over
intro_paragraphs: Coral Springs sold its first 536 lots in 1964 and reached residential build-out in 2003, which means the whole city is now a remodeling market rather than a construction one. Ranch and split-level houses in Ramblewood, Maplewood and Forest Hills are pushing fifty. The 1980s golf-course homes around Eagle Trace and the Coral Springs Country Club have good bones and dated everything else. Newer gated builds around Turtle Run, Wyndham Lakes and Cypress Run need less rescue and more editing. Whole-home remodeling here is mostly about correcting a floor plan drawn for a different decade.

Plan review, field inspections and final sign-off all sit with the City of Coral Springs Building Department; applications go in through the city's online permitting portal. Zoning sits with Community Development at City Hall on West Sample Road. Above the city, the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals administers building code county-wide: it reviews proposed amendments to the Florida Building and Fire Prevention codes, certifies building officials and inspectors, and issues formal interpretations when a code section is disputed. Broward also sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so impact windows and doors need HVHZ product approvals on file.

What that looks like on your street: a fixed written scope before anyone swings a hammer, a supervisor on site every day, and floor and finish protection through a house you still have to live near. Two decades of South Florida work and 150-plus remodels and additions later, we still pull every permit and take every inspection, which is a baseline rather than a boast. Our crews keep the driveway swept and the container where the association said it could sit, because in Coral Springs your neighbors notice. One team owns the job from estimate through warranty.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets demolished before the scope is written down. These are the pieces we most often combine on a Coral Springs whole-home project.

scope_items.name: Removing the 1970s walls
scope_items.desc: Taking down the partitions that boxed off kitchens and family rooms in older Coral Springs plans, with engineered beams and sealed calculations wherever block walls carry load.

scope_items.name: Full mechanical replacement
scope_items.desc: New panel and service, repiped supply and drain lines, and right-sized air conditioning for houses whose systems were specified when the trees were saplings.

scope_items.name: Reglazing the whole house
scope_items.desc: Window and door retrofits carrying High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approvals, permitted as their own scope and detailed so the stucco returns look deliberate.

scope_items.name: Exterior colors the city allows
scope_items.desc: Repainting from the city's approved palette and reroofing off its pre-approved tile list, so a finished remodel does not end with a code compliance notice on the door.

scope_items.name: Kitchen and bath integration
scope_items.desc: Rolling both rooms into one permit and one schedule so rough plumbing, waterproofing and stone fabrication land in sequence instead of three separate mobilizations.

faqs.q: Does Coral Springs really regulate what color I paint my house?
faqs.a: It regulates which colors will not get you a citation, which amounts to the same thing. Community Development publishes an approved exterior palette and expects a paint application before a house is repainted, so the selection is confirmed rather than discovered afterward. Strongly saturated and very dark shades generally fall outside it. If you also sit in an association, its palette narrows the field further, and the stricter of the two governs. We confirm the color against both lists before anyone orders material.

faqs.q: What is the realistic timeline on a gut renovation?
faqs.a: Design and engineering first, then plan review at the Building Department, then construction, and the front half is the part people underestimate. A straightforward interior gut can be permitted in weeks; anything structural takes longer. Construction on a full house commonly runs several months, more when custom cabinetry or an HOA architectural review sits in the path. You get a written schedule attached to the estimate and a supervisor whose job is defending it.

faqs.q: My HOA has architectural review. Who deals with that, me or you?
faqs.a: We assemble the submittal package and you sign it, because most associations will only accept an application from the owner of record. What we supply is what boards actually want: elevations, material and color selections, a site plan, and current license and insurance certificates. We also plan around gate access, delivery windows and quiet hours, which is the part that quietly wrecks other people's schedules in the gated sections.

faqs.q: Is my house structurally different from an older Miami home?
faqs.a: Mostly in age and detailing rather than in material. Coral Springs is concrete block and stucco like the rest of South Florida, but the housing stock starts in the mid-1960s, so you are typically working with tie-beam construction, original single-pane glazing, and occasionally aluminum branch wiring in the narrow band of houses built in the late 1960s and early 1970s. Block walls do make structural openings predictable once an engineer sizes the beam.

faqs.q: How much do Coral Springs gut renovations run?
faqs.a: Wide, and driven by how far past cosmetic the scope goes. Replacing mechanicals, moving walls and reglazing a house in impact units is a different order of project than new floors and paint. We would rather price a specification than a square-foot guess, so you get a fixed written number with real allowances. PGX competes on certainty and finish quality, not on being the cheapest of three bids, and we say so early.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the rooms that annoy you and the ones you would never touch. We answer with a scope, a schedule and a signable number, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Coral Springs Kitchen Remodeling, FL | PGX Builders Group
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Coral Springs kitchen remodeling that opens the load-bearing wall, then adds made-to-fit cabinetry and slab stone. Permits handled: (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Cabinetry, slab stone and load-bearing openings for Coral Springs kitchens, from Ramblewood ranches to Wyndham Lakes two-stories. Permitted through the city Building Department, inspected, and run day to day by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The kitchen the builder closed off
intro_paragraphs: Coral Springs kitchens have a generational problem. Houses from the city's first two decades, in Ramblewood, Maplewood, The Crossings and Westview, were built with galley kitchens walled off from the family room, because that is how 1972 thought about cooking. The 1980s and 1990s stock around Eagle Trace, Cypress Run and Wyndham Lakes opened up a little and then stopped. So kitchen remodeling here usually begins with a wall coming out, an island going in, and a real pantry appearing where a broom closet used to live.

Anything touching plumbing, gas, electrical or structure is permitted by the Coral Springs Building Department and inspected before drywall closes it up. If the scope changes a window or adds an exterior vent, Community Development's zoning review joins in. Water and sewer are not automatically the city's here either: depending on your address, service may come from the Coral Springs Improvement District, the North Springs Improvement District or the city's own utility, which matters when a remodel adds fixtures. Countywide, the Board of Rules and Appeals sets the code interpretations every reviewer works from.

Cabinet shops set the honest schedule on a high-end kitchen, so we order early and stage demolition around the delivery date rather than leaving you camped in a gutted room for a season. Stone is templated after the boxes are set and leveled, never before. Appliance specifications get checked against rough-in dimensions while changes are still free. The scope is fixed in writing, one supervisor answers the phone, and containment keeps drywall dust out of the rooms you are still living in. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: Inside a Coral Springs kitchen build
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Priced line by line and agreed before demolition. These five elements show up in nearly every kitchen we build on this side of Broward.

scope_items.name: Custom cabinetry, built to fit
scope_items.desc: Made-to-order boxes and doors finished for Florida humidity and sized to your real ceiling height, rather than a stock catalog that assumes eight feet everywhere.

scope_items.name: Islands and slab stone
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble or porcelain templated on site, with island framing engineered to carry the weight and any seating overhang supported rather than cantilevered on faith.

scope_items.name: Opening the load-bearing wall
scope_items.desc: Engineered beam, sealed calculations and a permit for removing the block wall that has separated your kitchen from everyone else since the house was built.

scope_items.name: Relocating gas and appliances
scope_items.desc: Appliances land where the plan needs them rather than where the old rough-ins sat, which means fresh gas runs, dedicated circuits and a vent path through the wall.

scope_items.name: Service capacity and lighting
scope_items.desc: Panel or service upgrades where an induction range, double ovens and a wine unit exceed what a 1970s Coral Springs house was wired to carry, plus layered lighting.

faqs.q: Can I take out the wall between my kitchen and living room?
faqs.a: Usually yes, and in Coral Springs block construction it is a well-understood move. An engineer determines whether the wall carries roof or floor load, sizes a beam or header, and seals the drawings that go to the Building Department with the permit application. Non-bearing partitions are simpler but still get permitted when plumbing or electrical runs inside them. What we will not do is open it first and work out the structure afterward.

faqs.q: Do I need my HOA's approval for an interior kitchen?
faqs.a: Usually not for work entirely inside the walls, but read your documents before assuming. Associations across Coral Springs govern contractor hours, parking, debris containers and gate access, and several require a certificate of insurance naming the association before a truck rolls in. If your kitchen adds a vent hood penetration through an exterior wall or changes a window, that does become an architectural review item. We sort out which applies at the first visit.

faqs.q: How long is a custom kitchen out of commission?
faqs.a: Plan around the cabinet lead time first. Good custom packages take a couple of months or more to fabricate, and that clock starts at final field measure, not at contract signing. On-site work for a full kitchen typically runs six to ten weeks once demolition begins, longer with a structural opening or a service upgrade. We sequence so the room comes out when the cabinets are close, not while they are still a drawing.

faqs.q: Is a high-end kitchen worth it in a production-built house?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Much of the Coral Springs housing stock is well-built block with generous footprints and unremarkable original finishes, which is a good starting point rather than a bad one. Custom cabinetry, real stone and a corrected layout change how the entire floor reads. Where we push back is on spending stone money in a room whose supply lines and electrical panel still need replacing. That order gets reversed.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a kitchen at this level?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone lead, appliances follow closely behind, and structural work is the variable that moves a number most. Rather than quote a range that means nothing, we measure, scope and price a specification you can hold us to. If the deciding factor is the lowest of three numbers, we are the wrong call, and we would rather say that in the first hour than the fourth month.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Send photos, or better, let us stand in the room with a tape measure. What follows is a scope with a price attached, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Primary Bath Remodeling in Coral Springs, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Coral Springs bath remodels: 1970s to 2000s homes get real waterproofing, curbless showers and stone that lasts. Licensed GC, (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, guest baths and powder rooms across Coral Springs, with frameless glass, stone, freestanding tubs and membranes that get flood-tested before tile. Permitted through the city Building Department and inspected at every rough.
intro_paragraphs: Ask a Coral Springs homeowner what bothers them and the bathroom answer arrives quickly. The city's original stock in Forest Hills, Maplewood and Ramblewood came with a hall bath and a modest primary, both planned around a sixty-inch tub and a single vanity. Even the roomier 1990s houses in Turtle Run and Wyndham Lakes handed you square footage without handing you a shower you would choose on purpose. Bathroom remodeling here is therefore a redistribution project: annexing a closet, shifting a doorway, and building the suite the plan never contained.

Permits come from the City of Coral Springs Building Department, and the inspection sequence of plumbing rough, electrical rough, then close-in is precisely why a properly built bath outlasts a cosmetic one. Adding or enlarging a window pulls in zoning review from Community Development, and any new exterior glazing carries a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approval because Broward is inside the HVHZ. Behind the walls, expect what the era handed you: cast iron or early plastic drains, copper or polybutylene supply on some houses, and slabs poured with no thought of a curbless entry.

A bathroom is the least forgiving room in a house and the easiest one to get quietly wrong. Membranes get flood-tested and held before a single tile is set. Slopes are verified with a level, heavy glass hangs on blocking installed while the walls were open, and niches get framed where you will actually reach for them. Every finished surface between the front door and the work zone is protected, because the rest of your house is not a job site. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, inspections signed off in order.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: What we rebuild behind the tile
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets ordered until the written scope is agreed, whether it is a powder room or a full suite. These are the pieces that decide whether it lasts.

scope_items.name: Borrowing a closet
scope_items.desc: Absorbing an adjacent closet or hallway to build a genuine primary suite, with framing, door relocation and plumbing rough-ins drawn and permitted as one job.

scope_items.name: Pans filled and held
scope_items.desc: Membrane pans filled and held before any tile goes down, with linear or point drains set to a slope we measure rather than estimate by eye.

scope_items.name: Curbless entries where possible
scope_items.desc: Recessing the pan into a slab or dropping second-floor framing when the structure allows, and saying plainly when a low curb is the better answer.

scope_items.name: Repiping while it is open
scope_items.desc: Replacing aging supply and drain lines during the same demolition, which is the only moment in a house's life when that work is genuinely inexpensive.

scope_items.name: Ventilation and layered light
scope_items.desc: A fan sized to the room and vented past the soffit, plus sconces at mirror height so nobody shaves under a single downlight.

faqs.q: Can I skip the permit if we are only replacing fixtures?
faqs.a: Swapping a faucet or a toilet in place, no permit needed. Anything that moves a drain, alters a supply line, changes electrical or adds ventilation, yes. The Coral Springs Building Department permits it and inspects it before it disappears behind cement board, and that sequence is worth having. It is also the paperwork a buyer's inspector looks for later, and retroactive permitting on a finished bathroom is an expensive way to learn this.

faqs.q: How do I know if my house has polybutylene supply lines?
faqs.a: Age plus a look under the sink usually answers it. Gray flexible plastic pipe with crimped fittings, common in houses built from the late 1970s into the mid-1990s, is the material people mean, and plenty of Coral Springs homes fall inside that window. If demolition exposes it, replacing that run while access is free costs a fraction of doing it after tile. We look before pricing and present it as a decision, not a surprise.

faqs.q: Will the city or my HOA care what I do inside a bathroom?
faqs.a: The city cares about code, not taste, so interior finish choices are yours. Your association cares about whatever spills outside: contractor parking, work hours, debris containers and, in the gated communities off Coral Ridge Drive and Riverside Drive, gate access lists and registered vehicles. If the scope adds or enlarges a window, that becomes an exterior change and both zoning review and architectural review can apply.

faqs.q: Can two bathrooms be remodeled at the same time?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is usually the cheaper way to get both. Shared demolition, one plumbing mobilization, one tile crew and one inspection cycle beat running the same project twice a year apart. The condition is keeping a working bathroom somewhere in the house, which most Coral Springs floor plans allow comfortably. We phase around whichever bath has to stay live and protect the route to it.

faqs.q: What actually drives the price of a primary bath?
faqs.a: Stone and glass are visible and expensive; the drains, supply lines, waterproofing and ventilation behind them are invisible and just as expensive. Layout changes that move plumbing cost more than layout changes that do not, and slab work costs more than framed floors. We price after seeing the space and understanding the building, and the number you sign is the number you pay unless something genuinely hidden turns up, documented in writing.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Fifteen minutes in the room tells us more than an hour of photographs. Book a walk-through and get a real scope, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions & Extensions, Coral Springs FL | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Home additions in Coral Springs, FL — rear extensions, second stories, in-law suites and garage conversions, engineered and fully permitted. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.hero_sub: Coral Springs houses grow four ways: out the back, up a floor, into the garage, or into a self-contained in-law suite. Engineered to Broward code, permitted through the city Building Department, supervised daily by a licensed general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Building out when the city is built out
intro_paragraphs: Coral Springs stopped producing new residential lots in 2003, which changed the arithmetic for anyone who likes their street. Families in Kensington, Cypress Run and Shadow Wood who need a fourth bedroom, a working office or somewhere for a parent to live are extending instead of moving. The projects repeat: a rear family room and primary suite behind a 1970s ranch, a second story over a single-level house on a lot with nowhere left to go sideways, a garage converted into legal conditioned space. Setbacks and lot coverage decide which one you get.

An addition is the most reviewed thing you can build here. Community Development checks setbacks, lot coverage and any variance need before the Coral Springs Building Department reviews structure, and a current survey plus sealed engineering is not optional. Foundations, tie-beams and roof tie-ins get designed rather than assumed. Every new window and door carries a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approval, since Broward sits inside the HVHZ, and the county Board of Rules and Appeals is the authority that settles a code interpretation when a reviewer and an engineer read the same section differently. Gated communities stack architectural review on top.

The hard part of an addition is the seam. Matching a stucco texture floated in 1978, tying a new roof plane into old trusses, blending a tile profile nobody manufactures anymore: that is where additions either announce themselves or disappear. We keep the occupied half of the house livable while the new half goes up, with dust walls, mechanical continuity and a supervisor on site daily. Scope fixed in writing before the first footing is dug. More than 150 remodels and additions delivered across South Florida, all of them permitted and inspected.
home-additions.scope_heading: Where the new square footage goes
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition begins with a survey, an engineer and a clear read on setbacks. Below are the five shapes that come up most across Coral Springs.

scope_items.name: Growing out the back
scope_items.desc: Family rooms, primary suites and enlarged kitchens added at the back on new footings, with tie-beam and roof joint drawn as a single package.

scope_items.name: Second stories
scope_items.desc: The existing footings and block are load-checked before anything is drawn, then a full upper floor goes on with stair, mechanical risers and a matched roofline.

scope_items.name: Garage conversions done legally
scope_items.desc: Turning a two-car garage into conditioned space with insulation, air conditioning, HVHZ-rated openings and parking resolved, so the square footage counts at resale.

scope_items.name: Quarters for a parent
scope_items.desc: Independent bedroom, bath and kitchenette space for long-stay family, built to code and scaled so it reads as part of the house rather than an attachment.

scope_items.name: Structural work below grade
scope_items.desc: Footings sized to the soil conditions, dowelling into existing foundations, and column work engineered before anyone puts a price on a finish.

faqs.q: How much of my lot can I actually build on?
faqs.a: That is a zoning question before it is a design question. Coral Springs regulates setbacks, lot coverage and height by zoning district, and Community Development is where the answer lives. Plenty of lots in the older sections have generous rear yards and easy room to extend; some of the tighter 1990s subdivisions do not. We pull the zoning parameters and read your survey before anyone pays for architectural drawings, so nobody designs a room that cannot legally exist.

faqs.q: Can my single-story house take a second floor?
faqs.a: An engineer decides that, and the answer usually depends on footings more than on walls. Existing foundations and block get evaluated against the new load, and where they fall short the design adds columns, pads or reinforcement. On many Coral Springs lots the arithmetic still favors going out: rear yards in the older sections are generous, and a ground-floor extension avoids re-roofing an entire house. We price both before you commit to drawings.

faqs.q: Does my HOA get a say in an addition?
faqs.a: In most of Coral Springs, yes, and it deserves to be taken seriously. Associations in the gated and golf-course neighborhoods review elevations, materials, roof tile and color before the city ever sees a plan, and some require the design to hold to the original builder's palette. A city permit does not override a recorded covenant. We treat architectural review as its own scheduled milestone instead of an afterthought that stalls a permit.

faqs.q: Does an addition mean re-roofing the whole house?
faqs.a: Not automatically, but plan for the conversation. Florida's roofing provisions govern how much of an existing roof can be altered before replacement comes into play, and tying a new plane into an old one on a house with discontinued tile often makes full replacement the cleaner outcome. Coral Springs also keeps a pre-approved list of roof tile colors and profiles for single-family homes, so matching is a selection question as much as a supply one.

faqs.q: Should we add on or move up to a bigger house?
faqs.a: It depends on how much the location is worth to you. In a city that reached build-out, the alternative usually means compromising on schools, commute or lot size, and transaction costs buy you no new square footage at all. Against that, an addition is months of design, review and living beside a job site. Before you pay for a single drawing, we will lay out the case against building as carefully as the case for it.

home-additions.cta_sub: Send the survey and tell us what the house is missing. You will hear about feasibility, the review path and the real number, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Summer Kitchens & Patios, Coral Springs FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Outdoor living in Coral Springs, FL — summer kitchens, covered patios, pergolas, pavers and screen enclosures, engineered and permitted. Call (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, covered patios, pergolas, screen enclosures and paver driveways for Coral Springs homes — engineered for hurricane loads, permitted through the city, and built by a licensed, insured general contractor who assembles the HOA package too.
outdoor-living.local_heading: The yard is the extra room
intro_paragraphs: The back yard is the cheapest square footage in Coral Springs and the least used. Lots here are generous by South Florida standards, particularly in the older sections along Riverside Drive and through Westview, and the golf and lake frontage around Eagle Trace, Wyndham Lakes and Cypress Run gives a lot of houses a view worth building toward. What owners want now is an outdoor room rather than a slab and a grill: a summer kitchen with real utilities, shade that survives a storm, and a pool deck that actually drains.

Outdoor living is where Coral Springs regulates hardest, because almost all of it is visible from somewhere. Patios and pool decks, screen enclosures, pergolas, driveway pavers, fences, retaining walls, gas systems, generators and even swale work each carry their own permit through the Coral Springs Building Department, and residential tree removal has a separate application. Exterior color has to land inside the city's approved palette, and roof tile has to come off the pre-approved list, so a covered patio roof is a selection with rules attached. Anything anchored is engineered for HVHZ wind loads.

We build outside to the standard we use inside. Gas, water and electrical for a summer kitchen are permitted trades, not weekend work. Cover and pergola footings are engineered and inspected before concrete. Deck drainage is planned so water leaves the house instead of collecting against the foundation, and materials are specified for sun, salt-laden air and chlorine rather than for a showroom photograph. Fixed written scope, one supervisor, and crews who keep staging tidy because your neighbors and your association are both paying attention. Lic. CGC1539072, licensed and insured.
outdoor-living.scope_heading: What the back yard actually gets
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One back yard, one permit set, one crew sequence. These are the elements Coral Springs homeowners most often combine into a single project.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens, properly plumbed
scope_items.desc: Permitted gas, water and electrical runs, cabinetry and counters rated for weather, and hood venting resolved properly rather than left for the roof to sort out.

scope_items.name: Covered patios and pergolas
scope_items.desc: Engineered footings, uplift connections and roof structures detailed for Broward wind loads, finished in tile or metal the city and your association will approve.

scope_items.name: Screen enclosures and pool decks
scope_items.desc: Aluminum enclosure structures anchored to sealed engineering, and deck slabs poured with slope and control joints planned so the surface sheds water away from the house.

scope_items.name: Pavers, driveways and swales
scope_items.desc: Driveway and walkway pavers permitted through the city, with the right-of-way swale restored to grade the way Public Works expects to find it afterward.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and terrace openings
scope_items.desc: Facade repair, repainting inside the approved palette, and sliding or French door replacement carrying High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals for the openings onto the terrace.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a pergola or an outdoor kitchen?
faqs.a: Yes, and usually more than one. The structure takes a building permit, the gas line takes a gas permit, the circuits take an electrical permit and the water line takes a plumbing permit. Coral Springs also permits screen enclosures, pool decks, driveway pavers, fences, retaining walls and generators separately. It is more paperwork than a covered patio looks like it deserves, and it is also why an appraiser and a future buyer treat the work as an asset.

faqs.q: Can I put a dark tile roof on a covered patio here?
faqs.a: Probably not, and this catches people late in the process. Coral Springs maintains a list of pre-approved roof tile colors and profiles for single-family homes, and tiles with heavy antiquing, very dark colors or high-contrast blends generally are not on it. Exterior paint works the same way, off the city's approved palette. Both are selection decisions with rules attached, so we confirm every one against the city list and your association's rules before anything is ordered.

faqs.q: How does HOA architectural review work for a backyard project?
faqs.a: Most Coral Springs associations want a submittal before the city does: a site plan showing the structure's footprint and distance to your property lines, elevations, materials, colors and the contractor's license and insurance. Approval times vary with each board's meeting calendar, which is why we start that clock in parallel with permit drawings rather than after them. In the gated communities we also register crews and vehicles for gate access.

faqs.q: Will a screen enclosure survive a hurricane?
faqs.a: A properly engineered and permitted one is designed to, which is a different sentence from a guarantee. Aluminum enclosures in Broward are engineered for High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads with specified anchor patterns into the deck and the host wall, and the inspection verifies those anchors before screen goes on. The failures people describe are usually old structures, undersized fasteners or work that was never permitted. Ask to see the engineering.

faqs.q: What does a full outdoor living project run?
faqs.a: Utilities and structure drive it far more than square footage does. A paver patio is one budget; a covered outdoor room with a summer kitchen, gas, water, power and a tile roof is genuinely another, and appliance and stone selections move the number as much as the footprint. We scope after walking the yard, checking how it drains and reading your association's rules, so the price reflects the project rather than a per-foot average.

outdoor-living.cta_heading: Come stand in the yard with us
outdoor-living.cta_sub: Show us where the shade should fall and where the grill should live. You get a drawn scope, a permit plan and a fixed number, in English o en español.
